overview_markdown:
Picobot is a minimalist, Go-based reimagining of the OpenClaw personal AI agent, packaged as a single ~9MB static binary with zero runtime dependencies. It delivers the core agent loop — persistent memory, tool calling, skills, and channel integrations for Telegram, Discord, Slack, and WhatsApp — while idling at roughly 10MB of RAM and booting almost instantly. All state lives in a `~/.picobot` directory, making backup and migration trivial.

Architecturally, it favors simplicity over extensibility: configuration is driven by environment variables and a config file, models are accessed via an OpenAI-compatible API (e.g., OpenRouter), and recent commits show active hardening work such as a configurable exec-command denylist, configurable agent timeouts applied across all channels, and improved onboarding safeguards. Docker images are published at ~29MB on Alpine, and the project builds cleanly from source with a single `go build`.

Compared to OpenClaw, Picobot deliberately sacrifices the rich plugin ecosystem and multi-process gateway architecture in exchange for operability on the cheapest hardware — a $5 VPS, a Raspberry Pi, or even an Android phone via Termux. It is best understood as the 'just enough agent' option: ideal for solo self-hosters who want a private, always-on chat agent without managing Python environments or heavyweight containers.
